t: A Berber religious reform movement from the Atlas Mountains that united the whole Maghreb and Muslim al-Andalus.
Its court patronised Averroes, whose Aristotle commentaries reshaped European scholastic thought.
Defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 shattered its prestige; the Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269.
dyk: Seville's Giralda, now the cathedral bell tower, was begun in 1184 as the minaret of the city's Almohad Great Mosque.
ev: Ibn Tumart is proclaimed the Mahdi by his followers in the Atlas Mountains
Abd al-Mu'min captures the Almoravid capital Marrakesh and takes the title of caliph
Almohads complete the conquest of the Maghreb from Morocco to Tunisia
Abu Yaqub Yusuf I absorbs the last independent Muslim principality of al-Andalus
Yaqub al-Mansur crushes Alfonso VIII of Castile at the Battle of Alarcos
Christian coalition shatters the Almohad army at Las Navas de Tolosa
Ferdinand III of Castile takes Seville
The last caliph, Idris al-Wathiq, is killed as the Marinids seize Marrakesh
